COBRA.definition: Cabinet Office Briefing Room A - UK Government's emergency response committee
COBRA.wiki: COBRA (Cabinet Office Briefing Room A) is the crisis response committee of the UK Government, convened to handle matters of national emergency or major disruption. Its meetings are typically held in the Cabinet Office buildings in London and are chaired by the Prime Minister or other senior ministers depending on the nature of the emergency.

NATO.wiki: An intergovernmental military alliance between North American and European countries. Its core principle is collective defence, enshrined in Article 5: an attack against one Ally is considered an attack against all.

NCSC.wiki: The UK Government's authority on cyber security, providing support to the most critical organizations in the UK, the wider public sector, industry, and the general public.

SWIFT.definition: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication
SWIFT.wiki: A vast messaging network used by financial institutions to securely transmit information and instructions through a standardized system of codes. Blocking a country from SWIFT is considered a severe financial sanction.

DDoS.wiki: A malicious attempt to disrupt the normal traffic of a targeted server, service or network by overwhelming the target or its surrounding infrastructure with a flood of Internet traffic.

GCHQ.wiki: An intelligence and security organization responsible for providing signals intelligence (SIGINT) and information assurance to the government and armed forces of the United Kingdom.

QEC.wiki: A class of two aircraft carriers of the Royal Navy. They are the largest and most powerful surface warships ever constructed for the Royal Navy, capable of carrying up to 40 aircraft including the F-35B Lightning II.

RIMPAC.wiki: The world's largest international maritime warfare exercise, hosted and administered by the United States Navy's Indo-Pacific Command. It is held biennially during June and July.

AUKUS.wiki: AUKUS is a trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States, announced in September 2021. Its primary focus is to support Australia in acquiring conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines (SSNs), but it also includes broader cooperation on advanced capabilities such as cyber, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, and undersea capabilities. It is widely viewed as an effort to counter China's growing influence in the Indo-Pacific region.

MOD.wiki: The British government department responsible for implementing the defence policy set by Her Majesty's Government, and is the headquarters of the British Armed Forces.

C2.wiki: The exercise of authority and direction by a properly designated commander over assigned and attached forces in the accomplishment of the mission.

UK.wiki: A sovereign country in Europe, off the north-western coast of the continental mainland, comprising England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.

US.wiki: A country primarily located in North America, consisting of 50 states and a federal district. It is a founding member of NATO and the UK's closest ally.

USA.wiki: A country primarily located in North America, consisting of 50 states and a federal district. It is a founding member of NATO and the UK's closest ally.

UN.wiki: An intergovernmental organization whose stated purposes are to maintain international peace and security, develop friendly relations among nations, achieve international cooperation, and be a centre for harmonizing the actions of nations.

Article 5.definition: NATO Article 5 - The principle of collective defence
Article 5.wiki: Article 5 is the cornerstone of NATO, stating that an armed attack against one or more of its members shall be considered an attack against them all. It has only been invoked once, following the 9/11 attacks in the US.

CDS.definition: Chief of the Defence Staff - The professional head of the British Armed Forces
CDS.wiki: The professional head of the British Armed Forces and the most senior uniformed military adviser to the Secretary of State for Defence and the Prime Minister.

PM.wiki: The head of the UK Government, ultimate decision-maker in national emergencies, and chair of the National Security Council and senior COBRA meetings.

RAF.wiki: The United Kingdom's air and space warfare service, responsible for air defence, strategic and tactical mobility, intelligence gathering, and precision strike capabilities.

HMS.definition: Her Majesty's Ship (or His Majesty's Ship)
HMS.wiki: The official ship prefix used for naval vessels in the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom.

HMNB.wiki: Designation for primary operating naval bases in the United Kingdom, including HMNB Clyde (Faslane/Coulport, home of the UK nuclear deterrent), Portsmouth, and Devonport.

QRA.wiki: State of readiness maintained 24/7 by RAF Typhoon fighter jets and aircrew at RAF Coningsby and RAF Lossiemouth to scramble within minutes and intercept unidentified or hostile aircraft approaching UK airspace.

ASW.wiki: Branch of naval warfare using surface warships, attack submarines, sonobuoys, and maritime patrol aircraft (such as the P-8A Poseidon) to locate, track, and counter hostile submarines.

GIUK.definition: Greenland, Iceland, and United Kingdom Gap
GIUK.wiki: A strategic naval chokepoint in the northern Atlantic Ocean through which Russian naval vessels and submarines based in the Northern Fleet must pass to access the open Atlantic.

CASD.wiki: Operation Relentless: the UK's continuous submarine patrol posture maintained without interruption since April 1969, ensuring at least one Royal Navy Vanguard-class ballistic missile submarine armed with Trident missiles is undetected at sea.

MACA.definition: Military Aid to the Civil Authorities
MACA.wiki: Operational framework under which the UK Armed Forces provide support and resources to civil authorities, police, or local government during emergencies, disaster relief, or major security disruptions.

GRU.wiki: The foreign military intelligence agency of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation, conducting covert operations, signals intelligence, sabotage, and cyber warfare.

JEF.wiki: A UK-led multinational military framework comprising ten northern European nations (UK, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden) designed for rapid response to regional crises.

GPS.wiki: A satellite-based radio navigation system owned and operated by the United States Space Force, critical for civilian navigation and military precision guidance.

EU.wiki: A supranational political and economic union of European nations with close security, trade, and diplomatic ties to the United Kingdom.

SSN.wiki: General-purpose attack submarines powered by nuclear reactors (such as the Royal Navy's Astute-class), specialized in hunting enemy surface vessels and submarines, land-attack missile strikes, and covert intelligence collection.

EEZ.wiki: An area of the sea in which a sovereign state has special rights regarding the exploration and use of marine resources, extending up to 200 nautical miles from its coastal baseline.
